transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because things at work have been getting strange for me. I’m a cashier, and at the register I keep getting stuck doing things that don’t really fit what’s happening—like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. Last week I got written up for it, so... I figured I needed to talk to someone.
Do you find that these actions, like tapping the scanner, come from a feeling that you have to do them a certain way to prevent something bad from happening or because you get anxious if you don't?

Not really like that, no. It doesn’t feel like I’m doing it to stop something bad from happening. It’s more like I just get stuck in it—like tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or my hand just freezes over the cash drawer even though the customer is right there waiting. It doesn’t match what’s going on, and I know it looks odd, but in the moment I have trouble moving on.
When these episodes happen at work, do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself or the world around you—like things feel unreal or you're observing yourself from outside your body?
I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t noticed feeling like I’m outside my body or that the store isn’t real. It’s more that I get stuck in what I’m doing, and it’s hard to shift out of it.
Outside of your work at the register, do you ever find yourself making repeated movements—like hand waving, rocking, or other body movements—that you don’t seem to be able to control?

Not really hand waving or rocking, no. The main thing I’ve noticed is at the register—getting stuck tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer when I should be helping the customer. That’s the kind of thing that’s been causing problems.
Before you find yourself tapping the scanner or freezing over the cash drawer, do you ever feel a strong inner tension or a need to do it a certain way before you can move on?

I don’t really feel a strong tension first, or like I have to do it a certain way to make things okay. It’s more that I just get stuck doing something that doesn’t fit the moment—like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or freezing with my hand over the cash drawer when the customer is waiting. That’s what got me written up last week.
Do you feel like you have control over these movements when they happen, or do they feel involuntary and out of your control?

It feels mostly out of my control when it happens. I don’t decide, “I’m going to tap the scanner now,” or stand there with my hand over the drawer. I just get stuck in it, and then I realize the customer is waiting and I’m not moving on like I should. That’s why it’s been a problem at work.
Have you ever experienced these kinds of movements or freezing in places or situations outside of work, like at home or when you're alone?

I haven’t really noticed it much outside of work. The main place it happens is at the register—like I get stuck tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. That’s what got me written up last week.
